// Part of the Dim Factory web starter. MIT License: copy, change and share it freely.
// The three states every part of a page that loads something needs: loading, empty and error. Each is written for
// the people using the site, says what is happening, and keeps the layout steady.
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'

export function Loading({ label = 'Loading…' }: { label?: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="state" role="status" aria-live="polite">
      <span className="spinner" aria-hidden="true" />
      <span>{label}</span>
    </div>
  )
}

export function Empty({ title, children }: { title: string; children?: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <div className="state state--empty">
      <p className="state__title">{title}</p>
      {children}
    </div>
  )
}

export function ErrorState({
  title = 'This part could not be loaded',
  message,
  onRetry,
}: {
  title?: string
  message?: string
  onRetry?: () => void
}) {
  return (
    <div className="state state--error" role="alert">
      <p className="state__title">{title}</p>
      {message !== undefined && <p className="state__detail">{message}</p>}
      {onRetry !== undefined && (
        <button type="button" className="button button--secondary" onClick={onRetry}>
          Try again
        </button>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
